conventions.convention: Stress is tension-positive: traction on outward normal n is σn; Lij=∂jui and stress divergence is rowwise.
D=(L+Lᵀ)/2, θ=tr D, D₀=D−θI₃/3, τ=2μD₀+ζθI₃, and λ=ζ−2μ/3. μ and ζ are nonnegative; λ need not be.
Fourier flux is q=−K∇T; K may be anisotropic and nonsymmetric, but sym K is positive semidefinite.
The adopted local state relation is C² on an open (v,s) domain, with v=1/ρ, T=e_s>0 and p=−e_v. Thermal-chart positivity and convexity are separate hypotheses.
Barotropic Euler is an unforced, positive-density C² model with P∈C¹((0,∞)); it imposes no sign on P′.
Incompressible pressure is a constraint multiplier, not thermodynamic equation-of-state pressure; density and shear viscosity are constant, with ρ₀>0 and μ≥0.

Entropy admissibility is a pointwise algebraic test with D and g independently varied, not an assertion that every tested pair is realized by a global solution. The Gibbs supplier's Countable Choice and balance hypotheses remain binding.
Acoustics is the pointwise first variation at ε=0, locally preserving positive density; c_s²=P′(ρ_b)=v_b²e_vv at fixed entropy. No finite-amplitude approximation bound follows.
Perfect-gas logarithms use dimensionless reference ratios. Entropy conservation requires τ=q=r=0, and the isentropic coefficient K(s₀) may differ between trajectories.
Closed kinetic energy uses either a fixed bounded C¹ domain with u=0 or a rectangular periodic cell with periodic fields and derivatives; nonincrease includes μ=0 and vanishing-strain cases.

load_bearing.statement: Adopt τ=2μ(ξ)D₀+ζ(ξ)θI₃, σ=−pI₃+τ, and q=−K(ξ)∇T, with specified nonnegative scalar laws μ,ζ and positive-semidefinite sym K. The viscous response is linear and rotationally equivariant; conductivity may be anisotropic.
The unforced branch has ρ=ρ₀>0 constant, div u=0, σ=−pI₃+2μD and ρ₀D_tu=div σ, with constant μ≥0, u∈C² and p∈C¹. Equivalently, ρ₀D_tu+∇p=μΔu.

Adopt e∈C² on an open state domain in (v,s), assign T=e_s, p=−e_v and ρ=1/v, and assume local material states have T>0. This is a pointwise local-equilibrium adoption, not a global inversion or convexity assumption.
For P∈C¹((0,∞)), positive C² density ρ and C² velocity u satisfy ∂tρ+div(ρu)=0 and ρ(∂tu+(u·∇)u)+∇P(ρ)=0. No sign of P′ is imposed.

Under the complete stated Gibbs state, motion, contact and balance hypotheses, including Countable Choice and T>0, G=(2μ|D₀|²+ζθ²)/T+(∇T)ᵀsym(K)∇T/T². The independently varied algebraic family is nonnegative for all symmetric D, all g and all T>0 exactly when μ,ζ≥0 and sym K is positive semidefinite.

For the stated fixed-entropy restriction of the C² local state relation, the first variation about (ρ_b,0) is δρ_t+ρ_b div w=0 and ρ_b w_t+c_s²∇δρ=0, with δρ_tt=c_s²Δδρ and c_s²=P′(ρ_b)=v_b²e_vv. If c_s²>0, the displayed cosine modes with ω=c_s|k| solve this linear system.

For the explicitly adopted calorically perfect state relation and complete Gibbs hypotheses, ρc_vD_tT=−pθ+τ:D−div q+ρr. On the additional branch τ=q=r=0, D_ts=0 and p=K(s₀)ρ^(1+R/c_v) along a trajectory of entropy s₀.
For an actual smooth unforced constant-density incompressible Newtonian solution with the stated fixed no-slip or periodic boundary conditions, E_k(t₂)+2μ∫[t₁,t₂]∫Ω|D|²=E_k(t₁) for every t₁<t₂ in I.

concerns.concern: Proof 2.1 passes from the local divergence identity to the integrated energy identity on a general bounded C¹ domain, citing only A2, step 1.1 and algebra. Its sole declared dependency is the model definition, which supplies no integration theorem. The opened local divergence supplier explicitly assumes Countable Choice, absent here. Declare an adequate integration supplier with its hypotheses, or supply the needed choice-free argument. The energy calculation itself is sound under the usual integration-by-parts justification.

The Statement refuted tests boundedness of |δρ(t,x)|+sqrt(Σ_i w_i(t,x)²), while explicitly assigning density and velocity different SI dimensions. This sum needs normalization by positive reference scales, an explicit numerical-coordinate convention, or separate componentwise boundedness conditions. The exponential witness and its mathematical unboundedness argument remain valid.

seams_checked.note: Frame, SI, traction and balance conventions match the opened suppliers. Gibbs consumers expressly retain the stronger smoothness, contact, continuity and Countable Choice hypotheses.

Linear isotropic classification, local state chart, Gibbs identity, coefficient iff and fixed-entropy response are used with their stated qualifications. No positivity of λ or global thermal inversion is inferred.
The scaling theorem separates incompressible multiplier pressure from barotropic pressure, selects constant μ, and adds P∈C² and positive reference response explicitly.

Exact-flow consumers use the constant-viscosity mechanical specialization. Creeping balance is explicitly an alternative zero-inertia assumption; conservative forcing in the Bernoulli consumer is separately assumed.

Periodic consumers explicitly construct the lower-dimensional invariant lifts into the three-dimensional stress model, select constant constitutive states and distinguish mechanical evolution from thermal balance.

Wall-power consumers distinguish the unforced model interface from their separately derived forced momentum equation. The acoustic consumer adds positive pressure response rather than attributing it to the base definition.

Forced and creeping branches are separately defined. The CFD consumer explicitly adopts its Sobolev weak extension and states that its regularity does not imply the classical model definition's C²/C¹ regularity.

The numerical gas postulate uses the same C² fundamental relation and derivative signs, with positive reference scales. Weak balance and entropy assumptions are separately adopted rather than inferred from smooth-flow deductions.

The closure consumers preserve constant density, viscosity, multiplier pressure and stress signs. Modeled covariance replacement and its dissipativity are distinguished from the exact Newtonian filtered covariance.
